title: Cholesterol Basics and Heart Health
summary: This quiz covers what cholesterol is and how LDL, HDL, and triglycerides affect health. It also explores testing, diet, lifestyle, and management of high cholesterol.

questions.q: Which type of cholesterol is called 'good' cholesterol because it helps carry extra cholesterol back to the liver?
o: LDL cholesterol
Triglycerides
HDL cholesterol
VLDL cholesterol
questions.tip: HDL is considered good cholesterol because it carries excess cholesterol from the blood to the liver to be removed.
questions.eli5: Think of HDL like a cleanup crew after family dinner, collecting leftover plates and taking them back to the kitchen.

questions.q: Which description best fits what cholesterol is?
o: A mineral like iron that helps carry oxygen in the blood
A sugar that dissolves easily in blood to give quick energy
A waxy, fat-like substance found in every cell of the body
A protein that fights germs and infections
questions.tip: Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance found in every cell of the body.
questions.eli5: Think of it like the wax on an apple skin — a fatty layer that is part of every tiny building block in your body.

questions.q: Where does most of the body's cholesterol come from?
o: Most is made by the liver, with the rest coming from food
Most is breathed in from the air, with the rest made by the lungs
Most comes from drinking water, with the rest made by the kidneys
Most comes only from food and the body cannot make it
questions.tip: The liver makes most of the body's cholesterol, with the rest coming from food.
questions.eli5: Like a bakery that bakes most of its own bread and buys just a little extra from a shop.

questions.q: Cholesterol does not mix with blood on its own. How does it travel through the bloodstream?
o: It dissolves directly like salt in water
It turns into sugar for transport
It is breathed out through the lungs
It is carried by particles called lipoproteins
questions.tip: Cholesterol does not dissolve in blood and is carried by particles called lipoproteins.
questions.eli5: Like oil in soup needs a delivery truck, fatty cholesterol needs lipoprotein carriers to ride through watery blood.

questions.q: Lipoproteins carry cholesterol in the blood. What does LDL (low-density lipoprotein) normally do?
o: Removes excess cholesterol and takes it back to the liver
Delivers cholesterol from the liver to cells, but excess can deposit in artery walls
Breaks down food in the stomach for digestion
Carries oxygen from the lungs to the body
questions.tip: LDL delivers cholesterol from the liver to cells, but excess LDL can deposit cholesterol in artery walls.
questions.eli5: Think of LDL like delivery vans from a warehouse — helpful in the right number, but too many clog the streets.

questions.q: What are triglycerides, which are often measured along with cholesterol?
o: A type of fat in the blood that provides energy, but high levels raise cardiovascular risk
A type of vitamin that strengthens bones and teeth
A type of red blood cell that fights infection
A type of hormone that controls sleep
questions.tip: Triglycerides are a type of fat in the blood that provides energy, but high levels raise cardiovascular risk.
questions.eli5: Like pantry jars of cooking oil saved for later meals — useful stored energy, but too many jars crowd the kitchen.

questions.q: Why is LDL often called 'bad' cholesterol?
o: Because it lowers blood sugar to dangerous levels
Because it prevents the body from absorbing vitamins
Because it causes immediate pain and fever
Because high levels can lead to plaque buildup in arteries
questions.tip: LDL is called bad cholesterol because high levels can lead to plaque buildup.
questions.eli5: Like grease poured down a sink drain, too much LDL can slowly clog the pipes that carry blood.

questions.q: Why is LDL cholesterol often called 'bad' cholesterol?
o: Because it helps clean extra cholesterol out of the blood
Because high levels can leave cholesterol in artery walls and form plaque (sticky buildup that narrows arteries)
Because it gives the body quick energy after meals
Because it lowers blood pressure and protects the heart
questions.tip: High LDL can deposit cholesterol in artery walls, leading to plaque buildup.
questions.eli5: Think of LDL like delivery trucks that dump extra boxes in the hallway when there are too many, blocking the way.

questions.q: What is the normal job of LDL in the body?
o: To carry oxygen from the lungs to body tissues
To carry extra cholesterol back to the liver for removal
To break down food in the stomach for digestion
To carry cholesterol from the liver out to cells that need it
questions.tip: LDL delivers cholesterol from the liver to cells, but excess LDL can deposit cholesterol in artery walls.
questions.eli5: Like a grocery van bringing supplies to houses, it is helpful until too many vans start piling bags on the street.

questions.q: Which eating pattern is most likely to raise LDL cholesterol?
o: Regular meals with fatty meats, butter, cheese, and full-fat dairy
Meals with oats, beans, lentils, fruits, and vegetables
Meals with vegetables, whole grains, and oily fish twice a week
Cooking with unsaturated oils instead of butter or lard
questions.tip: Saturated fats in fatty meats and full-fat dairy products can raise LDL cholesterol.
questions.eli5: It is like pouring bacon grease down a kitchen sink, over time the greasy stuff sticks and clogs the pipes.

questions.q: How would most adults know they have high LDL cholesterol?
o: They feel chest pain every time they eat fatty food
They notice yellow skin right after fatty meals
They usually feel fine and learn about it from a blood test called a lipid panel
They get dizzy only in the morning before breakfast
questions.tip: High cholesterol usually causes no symptoms and is found through blood testing.
questions.eli5: It is like dust building up inside a closed closet, you do not see it until you open the door and check.

questions.q: Which change to fats and fiber in the diet is widely recommended to help lower LDL cholesterol?
o: Eat more processed and fried foods made with trans fats
Limit saturated fat, avoid trans fat, and eat more soluble fiber from oats and beans
Replace fruits and vegetables with fatty meats and cheese
Skip whole grains and eat only full-fat dairy foods
questions.tip: Limiting saturated fat and avoiding trans fat while eating more fiber-rich foods helps lower LDL.
questions.eli5: It is like swapping heavy muddy boots for light sneakers and sweeping the path clean with a broom made of oats and beans.

questions.q: Over many years, what can high LDL cholesterol contribute to if it is not managed?
o: Plaque buildup in artery walls, raising the risk of heart disease and stroke
Stronger bones and healthier joints
Lower blood sugar and better eyesight
Faster healing of cuts and colds
questions.tip: High LDL can contribute to plaque buildup, increasing heart disease and stroke risk.
questions.eli5: Like rust slowly narrowing a water pipe, plaque narrows arteries so blood has trouble getting through.

questions.q: If two adults are similar except one has a higher HDL (good cholesterol) level, what is generally true about heart disease risk?
o: The person with higher HDL tends to have higher heart disease risk
The person with higher HDL tends to have lower heart disease risk
HDL level has no link to heart disease risk
Doctors ignore HDL and look only at age
questions.tip: Higher HDL levels are linked with lower heart disease risk, which is why HDL is called good cholesterol.
questions.eli5: Think of HDL like a cleanup crew after a school party — more helpers means less mess left to cause trouble.

questions.q: What does HDL stand for when doctors talk about good cholesterol?
o: High-density lipoprotein
High-dose lipoprotein
Heavy-density lipoprotein
High-density lipid
questions.tip: HDL stands for high-density lipoprotein, a particle that carries cholesterol in blood.
questions.eli5: Like a delivery van with its full company name on the side, HDL's full name tells you it is a dense carrier for cholesterol.

questions.q: You want to know your HDL (good cholesterol) number. Which blood test will include it?
o: Fasting blood sugar test
Thyroid hormone test
Complete blood count for anemia
Lipid panel or lipid profile
questions.tip: A lipid panel measures total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and triglycerides.
questions.eli5: A lipid panel is like a shopping receipt that lists each item separately — HDL is one line on that receipt.

questions.q: Total blood cholesterol is the sum of parts measured in a lipid panel. How does HDL fit into that total?
o: Total ignores HDL completely
Total counts only HDL
Total is HDL plus LDL plus part of the triglyceride level
Total is HDL minus LDL
questions.tip: Total blood cholesterol equals HDL plus LDL plus part of the triglyceride level.
questions.eli5: Think of total cholesterol like a grocery bill — HDL is one bag, LDL is another bag, plus a small snack from triglycerides.

questions.q: Which lifestyle pattern is most linked with maintaining a healthier HDL (good cholesterol) level?
o: Smoking daily and sitting most of the day
Regular physical activity and keeping a healthy body weight
Eating many foods high in trans fat
Gaining a lot of extra weight quickly
questions.tip: Regular physical activity and a healthy body weight are linked with healthier cholesterol levels.
questions.eli5: Like riding a bike often and keeping it clean keeps it running well, moving often and keeping a steady weight helps keep HDL healthy.

questions.q: LDL mainly delivers cholesterol from the liver out to cells in the body. In contrast, what does HDL mainly do?
o: Turn cholesterol into blood sugar for energy
Deliver extra oxygen to the heart muscle
Store cholesterol inside artery walls
Pick up excess cholesterol from blood and tissues and bring it back to the liver
questions.tip: HDL removes excess cholesterol from blood and tissues for transport back to the liver.
questions.eli5: If LDL trucks deliver boxes from the warehouse to houses, HDL trucks drive around town picking up extra boxes and returning them to the warehouse.

questions.q: A blood test shows high triglycerides, a type of fat in the blood. What does a high level usually mean for the heart and blood vessels?
o: It lowers the risk of heart disease
It raises the risk of cardiovascular disease
It has no effect on heart health
It protects arteries from plaque
questions.tip: High triglyceride levels raise cardiovascular risk.
questions.eli5: Like extra grease clogging a kitchen drain over time, extra triglycerides make heart problems more likely.

questions.q: A doctor orders a lipid panel, also called a cholesterol check. Which set of results will this test measure?
o: Blood sugar, iron, and vitamin D
Red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets
Blood pressure, heart rate, and body weight
Total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and triglycerides
questions.tip: A lipid panel measures total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and triglycerides.
questions.eli5: Like a four-item shopping list, a lipid panel always checks those four blood fats together.

questions.q: Total blood cholesterol is given as one number. How is that number calculated from HDL, LDL, and triglycerides?
o: HDL plus LDL plus part of the triglyceride level
HDL minus LDL minus the triglyceride level
The average of HDL, LDL, and triglycerides
LDL alone, without HDL or triglycerides
questions.tip: Total blood cholesterol is the sum of HDL and LDL plus part of the triglyceride level.
questions.eli5: Like a grocery bill that adds two big items plus a small part of a third, total cholesterol adds HDL, LDL, and a bit of triglycerides.

questions.q: People used to be told to fast, or eat nothing, for 9 to 12 hours before a lipid panel. Why was fasting especially recommended for triglycerides?
o: Because fasting permanently lowers HDL
Because fasting makes LDL disappear from the blood
Because a recent meal can temporarily raise triglycerides
Because fasting is needed to find plaque in arteries
questions.tip: Traditionally, fasting for 9 to 12 hours was recommended before a lipid panel, especially for triglycerides.
questions.eli5: Like stepping on a scale right after a big lunch, a recent meal can make the triglyceride number look temporarily higher.

questions.q: For a routine cholesterol screening today, what do most modern guidelines say about eating before the test?
o: You must always fast for 9 to 12 hours with no exceptions
Fasting is usually not needed because HDL, LDL, and total cholesterol barely change after a meal
You should eat a fatty meal right before to test digestion
You should skip the test if you ate at all in the past month
questions.tip: Most modern guidelines no longer require fasting before a routine lipid panel.
questions.eli5: Like checking shoe size after lunch, most cholesterol numbers barely move after eating, so fasting is often skipped.

questions.q: Which 2 habits are well known to raise triglyceride levels over time? (Choose 2)
o: Eating soluble fiber from oats, beans, and vegetables often
Getting regular physical activity and keeping a healthy weight
Regularly drinking sugary sodas and sweet drinks
Often drinking a lot of alcohol
questions.tip: Excess added sugars and excess alcohol are well-established causes of high triglycerides.
questions.eli5: Like pouring extra sugar and extra oil into the same pan, too many sweet drinks and too much alcohol overload the blood fats.

questions.q: Your lab report shows total cholesterol of 210 and HDL (good cholesterol) of 60. How is non-HDL cholesterol calculated from these numbers?
o: Subtract HDL from total: 210 minus 60 equals 150
Add total and HDL together: 210 plus 60 equals 270
Divide total by HDL: 210 divided by 60
Multiply total by HDL: 210 times 60
questions.tip: Non-HDL cholesterol equals total cholesterol minus HDL cholesterol.
questions.eli5: Think like a shopping bill minus a discount coupon — you take the total and take away the good part to see what is left.

questions.q: What is non-HDL cholesterol (the cholesterol number left after removing the good HDL part)?
o: Only the good HDL cholesterol that helps protect the heart
Only the triglycerides that were measured after fasting
All the cholesterol that is not HDL, including LDL and other artery-clogging types
Only the cholesterol that comes directly from food in the last meal
questions.tip: Non-HDL includes LDL plus other harmful cholesterol-carrying particles like VLDL.
questions.eli5: Think of a classroom without the helpers — non-HDL is everyone left who could cause trouble.

questions.q: Two adults both have a total cholesterol of 230. One has high HDL (good cholesterol) and normal LDL, while the other has low HDL and high LDL. What does this tell you about total cholesterol alone?
o: Total cholesterol alone always predicts the exact same heart risk for everyone
Total cholesterol alone can hide important differences, so you need the breakdown to judge risk
Total cholesterol alone proves the person with higher HDL has higher risk
Total cholesterol alone means diet and lifestyle do not matter
questions.tip: The same total can come from mostly good HDL or mostly bad LDL, so the breakdown matters.
questions.eli5: Like two lunchboxes with the same weight — one could be full of fruit and the other full of candy.

questions.q: If your LDL (bad cholesterol) rises a lot while your HDL (good cholesterol) and triglycerides stay about the same, what most likely happens to your total cholesterol?
o: It falls a lot because LDL and total move in opposite directions
It stays exactly the same because the body balances it
It turns into HDL so the total does not change
It rises because total includes LDL
questions.tip: Total cholesterol is the sum of HDL plus LDL plus part of triglycerides, so raising LDL raises the total.
questions.eli5: Like adding more apples to a fruit basket — the whole basket gets heavier.

questions.q: Why do many doctors track non-HDL cholesterol to judge heart disease risk?
o: Because it adds up all the cholesterol types that can build up in artery walls
Because it measures only the good HDL that cleans the blood
Because it shows blood sugar and iron levels at the same time
Because it tells exactly how much cholesterol you ate yesterday
questions.tip: Non-HDL captures all harmful, artery-clogging cholesterol particles, not just LDL.
questions.eli5: Like counting all the weeds in a garden, not just the tallest ones, to know the real work ahead.

questions.q: For most healthy adults age 20 and older, how often is cholesterol (total and related levels) generally advised to be checked?
o: Only once after age 65 and never again
Every day at home like body temperature
At least every 4 to 6 years if results have been normal
Only when chest pain or other symptoms appear
questions.tip: Adults 20 and older are generally advised to have cholesterol measured at least every 4 to 6 years.
questions.eli5: Like a car check-up every few years — you look under the hood before there is smoke.

questions.q: Your lab slip says 'lipid profile' and the nurse calls it a 'cholesterol check.' What does this mean?
o: They are three different heart scans
They are different names for the same blood test measuring cholesterol and triglycerides
The lipid profile measures blood sugar while the cholesterol check measures cholesterol
The cholesterol check is a urine test while the lipid profile is a blood test
questions.tip: Lipid panel, lipid profile, and cholesterol check are different names for the same test.
questions.eli5: Like fries and chips can mean the same food in different places, these three names mean the same blood test.

questions.q: A healthy 25-year-old adult had a normal cholesterol result. When is she generally advised to have it checked again if she has no new risks?
o: Only if she feels chest pain
Every week for a year
Only once after age 60
At least every 4 to 6 years
questions.tip: Adults ages 20 and older are generally advised to have cholesterol measured at least every 4 to 6 years.
questions.eli5: Like getting your car inspected every few years when it runs fine, cholesterol is rechecked every few years when it is normal.

questions.q: What happens to your body during a routine lipid panel for cholesterol testing?
o: A small sample of blood is taken, usually from a vein in the arm
A small piece of artery tissue is removed for testing
An X-ray picture is taken of the heart arteries
Electrical sensors are placed on the chest to record the heartbeat
questions.tip: A lipid panel is a blood test using a small blood sample, usually from an arm vein.
questions.eli5: Like taking a spoonful of soup to taste the whole pot, the lab takes a little blood to check fats in all your blood.

questions.q: A lipid panel reports total cholesterol plus separate HDL, LDL, and triglyceride numbers. Why are the separate numbers needed?
o: Because the lab machine cannot calculate a total number
Because total cholesterol alone changes every few minutes
Because insurance only pays for separate numbers
Because a normal total can still hide high LDL or low HDL
questions.tip: Total cholesterol alone can look normal while LDL is high or HDL is low, so the parts must be viewed separately.
questions.eli5: Like knowing the total grocery bill does not tell you if you bought veggies or candy, total cholesterol does not tell you the mix of good and bad types.

questions.q: For routine screening, modern labs often accept a blood sample after a normal meal. Why is the result still useful?
o: Food has no effect on any part of the blood
Eating makes all cholesterol leave the blood for hours
Total cholesterol, HDL, and LDL change very little after a meal
A meal makes the blood draw less painful
questions.tip: Total cholesterol, HDL, and LDL barely move after a meal, so routine screening is generally fine without fasting.
questions.eli5: Like adding a cup of water to a pool barely changes it, a meal barely changes most cholesterol numbers, only triglycerides bump up a bit.

questions.q: You are scheduled for a lipid panel (cholesterol test). Which 2 steps help make the results accurate? (Choose 2)
o: Follow the clinic's instructions about fasting or eating beforehand
Have a heavy fried meal and alcohol the night before
Tell the clinic about medicines, vitamins, and health conditions
Do intense exercise and drink lots of coffee right before the draw
questions.tip: Accurate lipid testing depends on following fasting/eating instructions and telling staff about medicines and conditions that affect lipids.
questions.eli5: Like following test rules and telling a teacher what help you used, you follow eating rules and share medicine info so the test is fair.

questions.q: Fatty beef, butter, and full-fat cheese can raise LDL (bad cholesterol). Which nutrient in these foods is mainly responsible?
o: Soluble fiber
Saturated fat
Vitamin C
Water
questions.tip: Saturated fats in fatty meats and full-fat dairy products can raise LDL cholesterol.
questions.eli5: Think of saturated fat like thick grease in a frying pan that can clog the drain if you pour in too much.

questions.q: Which foods are most likely to contain artificial trans fats, which doctors strongly discourage for cholesterol health?
o: Fresh apples and carrots
Plain brown rice and oats
Grilled chicken breast without skin
Store-bought cookies, pastries, and deep-fried fast foods
questions.tip: Trans fats in processed and fried foods are strongly discouraged for cholesterol management.
questions.eli5: Trans fats are like putting sand in a gas tank, they make the engine run worse, so it is best to avoid them.

questions.q: How does soluble fiber from foods like oats and beans help lower cholesterol?
o: It helps reduce how much cholesterol is absorbed from the gut into the blood
It adds extra cholesterol that the liver needs
It turns HDL (good cholesterol) into LDL (bad cholesterol)
It stops the liver from making blood cells
questions.tip: Soluble fiber from oats, beans, lentils, fruits, and vegetables helps reduce cholesterol absorption.
questions.eli5: Soluble fiber works like a sponge in your intestines, soaking up cholesterol so less gets into your blood.

questions.q: Olive oil, canola oil, nuts, and oily fish contain unsaturated fats. How do these fats compare to saturated and trans fats for heart health?
o: They raise LDL (bad cholesterol) much more than butter does
They should be avoided completely to manage cholesterol
They support better heart health when used instead of saturated and trans fats
They turn into harmful plaque faster than trans fats do
questions.tip: Replacing saturated and trans fats with unsaturated fats supports better heart health.
questions.eli5: It is like swapping heavy winter boots for light sneakers on a long walk, the lighter choice is easier on your body.

questions.q: Which 2 foods are good sources of soluble fiber that can help with cholesterol? (Choose 2)
o: Oatmeal and oat bran
White candy and soda
Beans and lentils
Bacon and pepperoni
questions.tip: Soluble fiber from oats, beans, lentils, fruits, and vegetables helps lower cholesterol.
questions.eli5: Oats and beans are like small brooms in your shopping cart that help sweep extra cholesterol out.

questions.q: Which weekly eating pattern best matches heart-healthy advice for cholesterol?
o: Fried chicken daily with sugary drinks
Lots of vegetables, fruits, and whole grains, with oily fish like salmon twice a week
Processed meats and pastries at most meals
Butter, cream, and fatty cheese at every meal

questions.eli5: This plate is like a colorful school lunchbox with garden veggies plus fish helpers visiting twice a week.

questions.q: Which foods are highest in saturated fat, the type of fat that can raise LDL (bad) cholesterol?
o: Olive oil, almonds, and salmon
Fatty beef, butter, cheese, and whole milk
Oats, beans, apples, and carrots
Fresh fruit, plain rice, and boiled potatoes

questions.q: Which foods are most likely to contain artificial trans fats?
o: Fresh apples and bananas
Plain beans and lentils
Grilled salmon and brown rice
Doughnuts, french fries, and stick margarine

questions.eli5: Like reused fryer oil at a fast-food shop, sweet packaged treats and deep-fried foods are the most likely hiding spots.

questions.q: If you eat a lot of saturated fat over time, what usually happens to your LDL (bad) cholesterol?
o: It goes up
It goes down
It stays exactly the same
It turns into HDL (good) cholesterol

questions.q: How do trans fats affect LDL (bad) cholesterol and HDL (good) cholesterol?

They raise LDL and lower HDL
They only change triglycerides for one hour after eating

questions.q: Which 2 swaps help replace saturated and trans fats with healthier unsaturated fats? (Choose 2)

Eat nuts or oily fish instead of fatty processed meats
Drink heavy cream instead of low-fat milk
Eat more fried pies made with shortening

questions.eli5: Like swapping heavy boots for light sneakers, swapping butter for olive oil and sausage for salmon is lighter work for the heart.

questions.q: You are checking an ingredient list to avoid trans fat. Which words tell you trans fat may be present?

Partially hydrogenated oils
Soluble fiber
Cold-pressed olive oil

questions.eli5: Like spotting a secret code word on a shopping list, seeing those two words tells you trans fat is hiding inside.

Butter, because it is dairy and natural
Olive oil, because it is mainly unsaturated fat
Lard, because it comes from meat

Whole grains keep more soluble fiber that helps reduce cholesterol absorption

Nuts provide unsaturated fats and fiber instead of harmful trans and saturated fats
Nuts contain artificial trans fats that raise good cholesterol
Nuts only help if they are heavily salted

Eat larger portions of fatty meats to stay full longer
Keep the same portions but add butter to vegetables
Avoid all fruits and grains so you can keep fatty meats

Whole fruit and juice have exactly the same fiber
Whole fruit keeps its soluble fiber while clear juice has most of the fiber removed
Whole fruit works only because the skin has trans fat

Tends to raise HDL (good cholesterol) and lower triglycerides
Removes all plaque already in artery walls
Stops the liver from making any cholesterol

Gaining a lot of extra weight always lowers heart risk no matter the cholesterol
Being active lets a person eat unlimited saturated and trans fat with no effect

o: Sitting most of the day and rarely moving
Doing one very hard workout every few months only
Resting completely for weeks to protect the heart
Being active with moderate effort, like brisk walking, on a regular basis

o: Helps raise HDL (good cholesterol)
Cures inherited very high LDL on its own
Helps lower triglycerides, a type of fat in the blood
Makes high cholesterol cause warning symptoms

o: Both will have exactly the same cholesterol numbers
The adult who sits most will always have higher HDL (good cholesterol)
The regularly active adult is more likely to have higher HDL and lower triglycerides
Activity only builds leg strength and does not affect blood fats

Cholesterol numbers stay exactly the same and only body weight changes

o: Belly fat has no link to blood fats and only affects height
